security_audit.summary: This skill is a documentation-only troubleshooting aid for Claude Code extensions. Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, local Claude path references, and official documentation links. Confirmed risks remain where the references tell users to display token values or print Claude session logs.

remediation.suggestion: Replace token echo commands with presence-only checks that never reveal full or partial secret values.
Avoid printing full Claude session files. Recommend targeted local searches and require redaction before any output is shared.
Add warnings near settings and MCP checks to redact local paths, permissions, server names, and environment references before sharing output.

static_findings.snippet: | Invalid JSON in settings | Validate with `jq '.' settings.json` |
| YAML invalid | Check frontmatter has `name:` and `description:` |
│      │      │  ├─ Missing ──► Set env vars or add to .env
| MCP connection fails | Test server manually with `npx` |
**See Also:** `claude-code-hooks` for hook debugging, `claude-code-templates` for correct structure

semantic_findings.title: Sensitive Token Display Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The debugging references instruct users to echo GitHub and Anthropic API token values. This can leak credentials into terminals, logs, copied bug reports, or chat transcripts.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited commands explicitly display token material, so the risk is semantic and intentional, not only a variable-name match.

semantic_findings.title: Sensitive Session Log Disclosure Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The debug commands tell users to print the most recent Claude session file. Session logs can contain prompts, tool outputs, local paths, and secret values.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command directly reads the latest file from the Claude sessions directory and prints it, which confirms session content disclosure risk.

content.value_statement: Claude Code extensions can fail because of file layout, frontmatter, permissions, hooks, agents, or MCP configuration. This skill gives practical diagnostic flows and command references for isolating the cause.
actual_capabilities: Diagnoses skill activation problems by checking file location, naming, frontmatter, and trigger descriptions.
Troubleshoots hook execution with matcher checks, executable permissions, JSON validation, and manual test guidance.
Inspects agent discovery and tool availability using Claude Code slash command workflows.
Reviews MCP connection problems, package availability, transport choices, and environment variable references.
Provides decision trees and command references for repeatable Claude Code extension debugging.
limitations: Some diagnostics require access to local project files or Claude configuration paths.
It does not automatically repair scripts, settings, or extension files without a separate user-approved edit.
Diagnostic output can contain sensitive local paths, settings, session data, or secrets unless redacted.
It focuses on Claude Code extension behavior, not general application debugging.

use_cases.title: Fix Skill Activation
use_cases.description: Find why a Claude Code skill does not load or activate by checking structure, metadata, and trigger wording.

use_cases.title: Trace Hook Failures
use_cases.description: Identify why a PreToolUse or PostToolUse hook is missing, not executable, mismatched, or returning the wrong exit code.

use_cases.title: Validate Agent and MCP Setup
use_cases.description: Check custom agent visibility and MCP server registration when Claude Code tools are unavailable or unstable.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Skill That Will Not Load
prompt_templates.prompt: Debug my Claude Code skill. The skill name is [name], it is located at [path], and the symptom is [what happens]. Start with file structure and frontmatter checks.

prompt_templates.title: Find Why a Hook Is Not Running
prompt_templates.prompt: Troubleshoot my Claude Code hook. The hook type is [PreToolUse or PostToolUse], the matcher is [matcher], and the script path is [path]. Check registration, permissions, input, and exit behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Agent or MCP Discovery
prompt_templates.prompt: Help diagnose why my Claude Code agent or MCP server is not available. Review the expected location, metadata, configuration entry, transport, and environment variable references.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Full Extension Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a diagnostic plan for my Claude Code setup. It includes skills, hooks, agents, MCP servers, and project settings. Prioritize checks that isolate loading, permission, and configuration failures.

output_examples.input: My hook appears in settings but never blocks a tool call.
output: Confirm the hook is registered for the exact tool name and event type.
Check that the script is executable and can read sample input from standard input.
Verify that blocking behavior uses the expected exit code and writes the message to the correct stream.

output_examples.input: My custom agent file exists, but Claude Code never selects it.
output: Verify that the agent file is in a supported user or project agent directory.
Check the frontmatter name and description for clear usage signals.
Use the agent list view to confirm discovery before testing delegation.

output_examples.input: An MCP server is configured, but its tools do not appear.
output: Test whether the server package can start outside Claude Code.
Review transport settings and referenced environment variables.
Confirm that permission rules allow the expected MCP tool names.

best_practices: Redact tokens, secrets, local paths, and session content before sharing diagnostic output.
Run checks from the intended project root and confirm scope before inspecting user-level configuration.
Start with Claude Code debug output, then verify structure, permissions, and metadata in order.
anti_patterns: Printing full API tokens or pasting raw session logs into a chat, issue, or support request.
Broadening tool permissions before checking deny rules, hook matchers, and exact command patterns.
Assuming an extension loaded before verifying filename, directory location, and frontmatter syntax.

faq.question: What problems does this skill help debug?
faq.answer: It helps debug Claude Code skills, hooks, agents, MCP servers, settings, permissions, and related extension loading behavior.

faq.question: Does it change my Claude Code configuration?
faq.answer: The skill provides diagnostic steps. Any configuration change should be reviewed and approved separately.

faq.question: Can it inspect global Claude settings?
faq.answer: Some examples inspect user-level Claude settings. Review and redact output before sharing it outside your machine.

faq.question: Is it safe to print API keys while debugging?
faq.answer: No. Use presence checks or redacted values instead of printing full or partial API keys.

faq.question: Can it help with MCP server failures?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers package checks, configuration entries, transport settings, environment references, and tool permissions.

faq.question: Does it replace official Claude Code documentation?
faq.answer: No. It organizes troubleshooting steps and links to official documentation for deeper reference.
